question: A shopkeeper sells 10 identical watches for ₹10,500, which is the cost price of 8 watches. Find his loss percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

10 watches SP = cost of 8 watches

So CP:SP ratio = 10 : 8

Loss = 2 parts out of 10

Loss% = (2 ÷ 10) × 100

**∴ Answer = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of 10 watches = ₹10500

Cost price of 8 watches = ₹10500

**Formula used:**

Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ CP of 1 watch = 10500 ÷ 8 = 1312.5

⇒ SP of 1 watch = 10500 ÷ 10 = 1050

⇒ Loss per watch = 1312.5 − 1050 = 262.5

⇒ Loss % = (262.5 ÷ 1312.5) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Formula

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 and Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Basic Relation

Loss = CP − SP and Profit = SP − CP

Ratio Method

If CP:SP is known, loss or profit can be found directly using ratio difference

Unitary Method

Find cost and selling price per unit first, then calculate total profit or loss
